# Dettifoss Short — Script Variations & Fact Sheet

**Footage you have:** wide/close shots of the waterfall + you crossing ice sheets to reach the viewing point.
**Format assumed:** vertical 9:16, ~30-35 seconds, platform-agnostic (Shorts/Reels/TikTok). Tell me if you want to tighten this for one platform specifically.

---

## 🎯 Fact Sheet (so you don't get "well actually'd" in the comments)

| Stat | Number |
|---|---|
| Average flow | 193 m³/s (~50,985 gallons/second) |
| Pool analogy | Fills an Olympic swimming pool (2,500 m³) every ~13 seconds |
| Peak summer flow | Can surge to ~400 m³/s during glacial melt (nearly double) |
| Drop / width | 44 m drop, 100 m wide |
| Location | Vatnajökull National Park, NE Iceland — fed by Vatnajökull, Europe's largest ice cap |

**Two ways to frame the superlative:**

- **Bold** (what most travel sites say): "the most powerful waterfall in Europe"
- **Bulletproof** (technically precise): "one of the most powerful waterfalls in Europe" or "Iceland's most powerful waterfall" — Wikipedia notes Rhine Falls edges it out on one specific metric, so this version is comment-proof.

The scripts below use the bold version — swap in the safer line if you'd rather not deal with pushback.

---

## Variation 1 — "Stat Attack" (Voiceover + Animated Numbers)

*Best for: YouTube Shorts/Reels, educational-viral audience, works with sound ON*

| Time | Visual | VO Script | On-screen animation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3s | Mist/close-up of falls | "Did you know the most powerful waterfall in Europe... is hiding in Iceland?" | Kinetic text: "EUROPE'S MOST POWERFUL WATERFALL" |
| 3-8s | You stepping onto the ice sheet | "This is Dettifoss. And to get here, I had to cross this." | Small location pin animation: "Iceland 🇮🇸" |
| 8-18s | Ice crossing, tension building | "One wrong step on this ice... and it's a very cold, very bad day." | Subtle shake/zoom on risky footsteps; no text (let it breathe) |
| 18-24s | Full waterfall reveal | "But then you see it. 193 cubic meters of water — crashing through here every single second." | Number count-up animation: 0 → 193 m³/s |
| 24-30s | Waterfall + graphic overlay | "That's over 50,000 gallons a second. Enough to fill an Olympic pool... every 13 seconds." | Animated pool icon filling up in a 13-second loop bar |
| 30-35s | You, smiling, waterfall behind | "This is just one of Iceland's insane waterfalls. Follow for more." | End card: "Follow for more 🌊" |

---

## Variation 2 — "Silent Scroll-Stopper" (Text-Only, No Voice)

*Best for: TikTok / muted autoplay feeds (~85% of viewers watch without sound)*

| Time | Visual | On-screen text |
|---|---|---|
| 0-2s | Waterfall wide shot | "Europe's most powerful waterfall 🌊" |
| 2-5s | Same shot | "...is in Iceland." |
| 5-6s | Cut to ice sheet | "To reach it, you cross this ⚠️" |
| 6-16s | Ice crossing footage | (minimal text — let tension play out) small caption: "no ropes. no guide. just ice." |
| 16-20s | Waterfall reveal | "193 m³/s" |
| 20-24s | Same | "= 51,000 gallons. Every. Second." |
| 24-28s | Same, pool icon graphic | "= 1 Olympic pool every 13 seconds 🏊" |
| 28-32s | Wide final shot | "Dettifoss, Iceland 🇮🇸 — save this for your trip" |

*Audio: don't hardcode a specific trending sound here since trends turn over fast — check your platform's trending-sounds page for a "big build / bass-drop" style track and time the drop to the 16s reveal.*

---

## Variation 3 — "The Risky Crossing" (First-Person Narrative)

*Best for: adventure/personal-brand audience — leans on curiosity/risk instead of the fact-hook, tends to pull higher watch-through because it delays the payoff*

| Time | Visual | VO Script |

| 0-2s | Mid-crossing, unstable footing | "I nearly went into the water to get this shot." |
| 2-8s | Ice crossing | "This ice sheet was the only way to the viewing point — and it was moving." |
| 8-16s | More crossing, close on feet/ice cracks | "No rope. No guide. Just me, a canyon, and a waterfall that fills an Olympic pool every 13 seconds." |
| 16-24s | Big reveal, wide shot | "This is Dettifoss — the most powerful waterfall in Europe. 193,000 liters a second." |
| 24-30s | You, catching breath, smiling | "Worth every second on that ice." |
| 30-35s | Final shot, direct to camera | "Would you cross this for the shot? 👇" |

blueprint_json.verified_facts_intro: This one has real narrative weight (poverty and sacrifice, then betrayal), and the facts hold up. The lepton ("widow's mite") was the smallest coin circulating in Judea — two lepta made one Roman quadrans, worth about six minutes of an average day's wage. The Tyrian shekel was the only currency the Second Temple accepted for its annual tax, prized for its ~92-94% silver purity, yet stamped with the pagan god Melqart and an eagle. On the "30 pieces of silver," scholars disagree on the exact coin type (Tyrian shekels are most likely, but Antioch staters or Ptolemaic tetradrachms are alternatives), so "historians believe / most likely" is the honest framing rather than a flat claim. Thirty shekels was also the Exodus 21:32 price of a slave — meaning Judas was paid the price of a slave.

fact_sheet.label: Lepton ("widow's mite")
fact_sheet.value: Smallest coin in circulation in Judea. Two lepta = 1 Roman quadrans (smallest Roman coin). Worth ~6 minutes of an average day's wage. First minted under Hasmonean king Alexander Jannaeus (103-76 BC) — already ~100 years old by Jesus's time, still circulating. Referenced in Mark 12:41-44 / Luke 21:1-4.

fact_sheet.label: Tyrian shekel
fact_sheet.value: The only coin the Second Temple accepted for the annual temple tax, because of its consistently high silver purity (~92-94%). Ironic twist: it's stamped with Melqart, a Tyrian pagan god, and an eagle — pagan imagery required for a Jewish religious payment.

fact_sheet.label: The "30 pieces of silver" link
fact_sheet.value: Most likely — but not certain — Tyrian shekels. Scholars also consider Antioch staters or Ptolemaic tetradrachms, since Matthew's Greek just says "silver coins." Use hedged language ("historians believe," "most likely") rather than a flat claim.

fact_sheet.label: Bonus detail
fact_sheet.value: 30 shekels was also the compensation set in Exodus 21:32 for a gored slave — meaning Judas was paid the price of a slave. Strong closing beat if you want it.

claim_framings.bulletproof: Historians believe this type of coin — the Tyrian shekel — is the most likely candidate for the thirty pieces of silver, though Matthew's Greek only says "silver coins."
claim_framings.note: History/Bible audiences fact-check hard — hedged wording ("historians believe," "most likely") keeps you accurate and reads as the kind of nuance the audience respects, instead of undercutting the hook.

# "Ancient Coins of the Temple" Short — Script Variations & Fact Sheet

**Footage you have:** merchant places 2 mites in your hand ("you are holding 2 mites") → later hands you silver shekels to inspect.
**Structure this gives you for free:** a two-act emotional arc — Act 1 = sacrifice/poverty (widow's mite), Act 2 = betrayal (temple tax shekel). Lean into that; it's a stronger arc than either coin alone.
**Format assumed:** vertical 9:16, ~35-40s (slightly longer than Dettifoss since there are two "reveals" to earn).

---

## 🎯 Fact Sheet

| Coin | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **Lepton ("widow's mite")** | Smallest coin in circulation in Judea. Two lepta = 1 Roman quadrans (smallest Roman coin). Worth ~6 minutes of an average day's wage. First minted under Hasmonean king Alexander Jannaeus (103-76 BC) — already ~100 years old by Jesus's time, still circulating. Referenced in Mark 12:41-44 / Luke 21:1-4. |
| **Tyrian shekel** | The *only* coin the Second Temple accepted for the annual temple tax, because of its consistently high silver purity (~92-94%). Ironic twist: it's stamped with Melqart, a Tyrian pagan god, and an eagle — pagan imagery required for a Jewish religious payment. |
| **The "30 pieces of silver" link** | Most likely — but not certain — Tyrian shekels. Scholars also consider Antioch staters or Ptolemaic tetradrachms as alternatives, since Matthew's Greek just says "silver coins." Use hedged language ("historians believe," "most likely") rather than a flat claim — this keeps you accurate *and* it's the kind of nuance history audiences respect. |
| **Bonus detail** | 30 shekels was also the compensation set in Exodus 21:32 for a gored slave — meaning Judas was paid the price of a slave. Strong closing beat if you want it. |

**Claim framing:**
- **Bold:** "This is the exact coin that paid for Judas's betrayal — thirty pieces of silver."
- **Bulletproof:** "Historians believe this type of coin — the Tyrian shekel — is the most likely candidate for the thirty pieces of silver, though Matthew's Greek only says 'silver coins.'"
